title: The Great Purge
log: 2026-11-01T08:04:35Z match: Claude Haiku 5.5 found no bank point the same, so it is written new

match.reason: The bank point covers Stalin's whole dictatorship (cult of personality, industrialisation, and terror), so the Great Purge is only one part of it and the card is broader than the focused new point, which is a close but broader match.

draft.title: The Great Purge
card: The Great Purge was a campaign of terror in the Soviet Union in the late 1930s. It was led by Joseph Stalin, the Soviet leader.
The secret police, the NKVD, arrested huge numbers of people accused of disloyalty. Many were pressed into confessing.
Some were put on public show trials. Many were sent to labour camps, and many were shot.
Party members, army officers and ordinary citizens were all targeted. The purge spread fear and removed people who might oppose Stalin.
draft.remember: The Great Purge used the secret police to remove people accused of disloyalty and to spread fear.

a.q: Who carried out the arrests during the Great Purge?
opts: The NKVD, the Soviet secret police
The Gestapo, the German secret police
The Red Army, the Soviet military
a.why: The NKVD made the arrests on charges of disloyalty. The Gestapo was the German secret police and had no role in the Soviet Union. The Politburo set policy, but it did not carry out arrests.
a.clue: Think of the Soviet secret police.

b.q: Anya, a Soviet factory worker in 1937, is arrested after a neighbour says she criticised Stalin. What is the most likely result?
opts: She is pressed to confess and sent to a labour camp
She is promoted for her honesty
She is freed after a fair public trial
She is sent abroad as a diplomat
b.why: During the purge, people accused of disloyalty were often pressed to confess and then jailed or sent to labour camps. A fair trial was unlikely. Many ordinary citizens, not only officials, were targeted.
b.clue: Think about what happened to people accused of disloyalty.

a.best: The NKVD, the Soviet secret police

b.best: She is pressed to confess and sent to a labour camp

Only one option is plausible, which makes the question too easy for Year 11.

proposal.title: The Great Purge
card: The Great Purge was a campaign of terror in the Soviet Union in the late 1930s. It was led by Joseph Stalin, the Soviet leader.
The secret police, the NKVD, arrested huge numbers of people accused of disloyalty. Many were pressed into confessing.
Some were put on public show trials. Many were sent to labour camps, and many were shot.
Party members, army officers and ordinary citizens were all targeted. The purge spread fear and removed people who might oppose Stalin.
proposal.remember: The Great Purge used the secret police to remove people accused of disloyalty and to spread fear.

a.q: Who carried out the arrests during the Great Purge?
opts: The NKVD, the Soviet secret police
The Gestapo, the German secret police
The Red Army, the Soviet military
a.why: The NKVD made the arrests on charges of disloyalty. The Red Army was a target of the purge, not the force making arrests, as many of its officers were seized. The Gestapo was the German secret police and had no role in the Soviet Union.
a.clue: One group on this list belongs to another country, and one was a target.

b.q: Anya, a factory worker in 1937, is not a Party member. A neighbour tells the NKVD she criticised Stalin. What is most likely?
opts: She is arrested, as ordinary citizens were targeted too
She is ignored, as only Party members were targeted
She is warned, as only army officers faced arrest
She is ignored, as only Stalin's rivals were at risk
b.why: The purge reached far beyond the Party and the army: ordinary citizens accused of disloyalty were arrested too. The tempting idea that only Party members or Stalin's rivals were at risk is wrong, since anyone reported for disloyalty could be seized.
b.clue: Look at which groups the purge reached.
